title: QWATT evidence batch
description: The unit of evidence that gets published and, when accepted, anchored on Stellar. Contains the accepted interval records it vouches for. `sha256` is computed over the canonical JSON of the batch with `sha256` removed. All energies are integers in milliwatt-hours so the canonical bytes are identical in every language. Defined in docs/ARCHITECTURE-FREEZE.md §2. Version 1.1.0 (week 2, V3-5) makes samples_root required.

seq.description: Batch sequence per site, strictly increasing.

spec_version.description: gates.spec.json version that judged every interval in this batch.

schema_version.description: interval.schema.json version of the contained records.

interval_count.description: Intervals judged in this window, accepted + rejected.

intervals.description: The accepted interval records, in sequence order. Rejected intervals are in the rejected ledger, never here.

intervals_root.description: Merkle root (SHA-256, odd node duplicated) over the canonical JSON of each interval.

samples_root.description: Required since batch schema 1.1.0 (V3-5): a fingerprint of every raw reading behind the window. The payloads are published at raw/<batch_id>.jsonl. R1, payload entry: {n, utf8} or {n, hex}. Its bytes are the UTF-8 of utf8, or hex decoded (lowercase, whole bytes); n >= 1 is the number of consecutive samples of the interval that arrived with exactly these bytes. CSV: the row as read plus "\n", one entry per row, n = the meters with a reading. HTTP POST /samples: the request body, as utf8 when its bytes round-trip as UTF-8, otherwise hex; n = its samples in the interval. Modbus: the reply frames of one poll, concatenated, as hex, n 1. POST /intervals: the request body, n 1. R2, binding: SHA-256 of the stream (each entry's bytes n times, in order) equals the interval's source.raw_sha256. Exempt: an interval with no source.raw_sha256; a record posted whole (source.adapter http-json) that kept its node's raw_sha256, whose one payload (n 1, utf8) is that record as posted (the same canonical JSON apart from clock_skew_s). An accepted or gate-refused interval needs a non-empty bound payload list; a line refused at the door is published with what came with it (no payloads when those were malformed). R3, raw line: canonical JSON of {"payloads":[...],"seq":seq or null,"ts_start":ts_start or null,"verdict":"accept"|"reject"} plus "\n" (seq only if a safe integer, ts_start only if a string). Exactly interval_count lines, sorted by Date.parse(ts_start) ascending (unreadable last), an accepted line before a refused one at the same start, otherwise in judgment order. R4: the intervals_root pairing (parent = SHA-256 of the two hex strings concatenated, an odd node paired with itself, no leaves = SHA-256 of no bytes) over SHA-256(bytes) of every payload entry of every raw line, in file order. Neither n nor the encoding enters a leaf.

energy_mwh.description: Sum over accepted intervals of the counted energy (min of the two meters, or the single meter), milliwatt-hours.

cumulative_mwh.description: Site total since genesis, after this batch.

prev_hash.description: sha256 of the previous batch, or 64 zeros for the first.
